text:
maria-g: Ran a 4xA100 Nsight capture for the 32k token stress run. seeing a recurring 10-18ms hole between GEMM and the NCCL all-reduce. attaching quick notes and the heatmap link: https://internal/heatmaps/1795832100.png

jason: can you paste the nv-nsight command and the metric set you used?

maria-g: sure — used timeline + sm__cycles_active.avg.pct, sm__pipe_tensor_cycles_active.avg.pct, lts__t_sectors_miss.sum, dram__throughput.avg.pct, and nccl latency from our nvtx markers. command: ```nv-nsight-cu-cli --events sm__cycles_active.avg.pct,sm__pipe_tensor_cycles_active.avg.pct --metrics dram__throughput.avg.pct,lts__t_sectors_miss.sum --csv --output capture_32k.csv ./run_inference.sh```

lee: quick thought: is KV-cache warmup causing an unexpected cross-rank barrier? If rank 0 serves a cache miss it might serialize fetches then trigger all-reduce with different start times.

ankur: looked at our custom timers (start_op / end_op) — they show repeated gaps aligned to the all-reduce start times. sample: op0 matmul end -> 0.7ms idle -> nccl allreduce start. gap distribution: [0.8, 1.2, 11.0, 15.3, 0.9] ms. the 11/15ms ones correlate with larger KV cache evictions.

maria-g: interesting. the nsight capture shows SM stalls but also stream synchronization points where work is enqueued on the wrong stream. suspect kernel selection fallback to TF32/FP32 path for some layers (quantized kernels had fast path, but a few layers used unfused kernels).

jason: any evidence of kernel selection flip? grep the capture CSV for kernel names and precision.

maria-g: yes — kernel list snippet: ```layer_42_matmul_fp16_fused  0.92ms; layer_43_matmul_fp32_unfused 12.4ms; layer_44_matmul_fp16_fused 0.91ms``` so we get an outlier FP32 unfused in the middle of FP16 stream. that + NCCL kick produces the big hole.

lee: that could be from our heuristic: if tensor shape > threshold or workspace allocation fails we fall back to unfused kernel. Was there an OOM or allocation retry logged? check allocator events.

ankur: checked logs — there are transient allocation retries on GPU1 when batch spikes > 48. allocator reports 6 retries at 8MB granularity. nvprof also shows cudaMallocAsync cost spike at ~14ms at same timestamps.

maria-g: hypothesis: batch heuristic + KV-cache miss pattern -> sudden larger workspace needed -> kernel selector picks unfused FP32 path -> kernel runs longer -> next NCCL all-reduce waits (comm/compute overlap lost).

jason: proposed fixes: 1) make kernel selector prefer fused FP16 kernels if workspace allocation would trigger allocation retries (pre-reserve), 2) smooth batching spikes by capping per-device inflight sequences, 3) add NVTX markers around allocator/memory fallback so we can spot it in timeline.

lee: also request adding per-stream timestamping for NCCL ops (ncclCommEnqueue time vs kernel enqueue time) to compute real comm/compute overlap ratio. current metric is too coarse.

ankur: I'll run an nvprof profile with `--profile-from-start off` and instrumented NVTX around allocator and selection code. command I'll run: ```nvprof --print-gpu-trace --profile-child-processes --csv ./run_instrumented.sh``` will push new capture to /tmp/prof_1795832.csv

perfbot: automated check — last 7 runs, comm/compute overlap pct dropped from 84% -> 61% when batch >48 and when KV cache miss rate > 6%.

maria-g: thanks — next steps: ankur to run instrumented capture (nvprof + nvtx), jason to add pre-reserve patch to kernel selector (small config flag), lee to add per-stream NCCL timestamps to perf counters. we should reconvene after one reproduce capture.

jason: grabbing the patch branch now, will run unit verify. ETA today EOD.

ankur: starting capture now. I'll drop the CSV and a short timeline GIF in the thread when done.

lee: FYI adding the per-stream timestamps will let us compute the comm/compute overlap as: overlap = sum(min(kernel_run, comm_run_window))/total_comm_time. we can then alert when overlap < 70%.

maria-g: perfect — if overlap alarm triggers we'll auto-fallback to a lower batch cap and force fp16 fused kernel preference. that should mitigate regressions until a proper selector fix lands.

jason: one more ask — can we add the allocator retry count to token-level tracing? small change but helps root cause.

maria-g: agreed. good runway. pinging when ankur posts capture. :eyes:
